title: S2h external skill hardening: structured risk report at inspection (scripts, endpoints, tools, credential references, dependencies, filesystem) gating quarantined to testing (P21)
spec:
orchestrator/skill_discovery.inspect(): extend the report with risk = {scripts: [{path, shebang or extension, executable bit}], endpoints: [hosts and URLs found in any file], tools: [names from the skill frontmatter allowed-tools or tools fields and Bash/shell mentions], credential_refs: [environment variable names matching KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|CREDENTIAL|AUTH and mentions of dotenv or credential files, names only], dependencies: [packages from requirements, pyproject, package.json, pip or npm install lines], filesystem: [absolute paths, home-directory references, recursive delete or chmod commands], scan: the context_scanner verdict per file from S1d, level: low|medium|high with reasons}. Level rules: high when scan is blocked anywhere, or an endpoint plus a credential_ref both appear, or a recursive delete or permission change appears, or a dependency is installed from a URL or git source; medium when any script, endpoint, dependency or credential_ref exists; low otherwise. Persist the report next to the quarantine content as inspection.json (reserved name check like the existing quarantine report filename rule). orchestrator/skills_registry.transition(): a quarantined skill may move to testing only when its latest inspection report exists, its content hash matches, and level is not high and scan is not blocked; otherwise raise ValueError naming the reasons unless the transition reason starts with 'human-reviewed:' (record that in the state document). CLI: `orchestrator skills inspect <id>` prints the risk report; `skills list` shows the level. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/14-skill-hardening.md.
Spec review T-1122 folded in: (1) No new file: the risk report is a new top-level key risk inside the existing findings.json (the file the tests already assert), so the content-hash listings in inspect(), check_upstream() and skills_registry._testing_findings() need no change; drop every mention of inspection.json. (2) The level gate WRAPS the existing _testing_findings() control rather than replacing it: the old blocks (block-severity finding, presence of a script) stay exactly as today, the new rule adds a block when level is high or scan_overall is blocked, and the existing 'override:' reason prefix keeps working alongside 'human-reviewed:' (both bypass, both recorded in the state document with the reason). (3) rollback() re-enters testing through the same wrapped gate, so both paths apply one bar; existing tests at tests/test_skill_discovery.py that assert findings.json content equality keep passing (extend their expected dicts with the risk key where they compare whole reports).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_risk_report_levels_from_fixture_skills (a benign skill low, a script-plus-endpoint skill medium, an endpoint-plus-credential skill high, a blocked-scan skill high)

tests/test_skills_registry.py::test_rollback_uses_the_same_wrapped_gate (a high-risk skill cannot re-enter testing via rollback without an override or human-reviewed reason; a script-only skill is still blocked as before)

spec_review_risks.issue: Base spec text still says: 'Persist the report next to the quarantine content as inspection.json (reserved name check like the existing quarantine report filename rule)', but the folded-in T-1122 review correction (1) explicitly says 'No new file... drop every mention of inspection.json.' The contradiction is still present verbatim in the packet sent to the executor. tests/test_skill_discovery.py:155 already asserts inspect() output equals the whole findings.json content, so a literal reading of the un-struck sentence would make an executor add a second file and break that assertion / diverge from the corrected design.

rollback() re-enters testing via `_testing_findings(skill_id, current, f"rollback: {last['reason']}", root)` (line 408), which prefixes 'rollback: ' onto the stored reason. If the original approval reason was 'override: ...' or 'human-reviewed: ...', the rebuilt reason no longer starts with either bypass prefix, so `_testing_findings`'s `reason.startswith(...)` checks fail and a previously-approved skill gets re-blocked on rollback. The new acceptance test only exercises the block-without-override case, so it won't catch this, but the spec's claim that 'both paths apply one bar' understates that legitimate override/human-reviewed rollbacks are already broken by this prefix concatenation.

'skills list shows the level' has no defined fallback for skills with no inspection report at all (builtin/active skills from sync(), or discovered/external skills never inspected) — there is no risk report to read since level lives in the quarantine-scoped findings.json, not the registry record. Spec should say what to print in that case (e.g. '-') so the executor and reviewer don't diverge; no acceptance test currently pins this down.

The risk object is asked to include `scan` (context_scanner verdict per file), which duplicates the pre-existing top-level `scan`/`scan_overall` keys already produced by inspect(). Spec should say to alias/copy the existing computed scan dict into `risk.scan` rather than implying a second independent computation, to avoid the two ever drifting apart.
